One-page data and methodology note

How this decision tool was built

Decision question. Which business categories and storefront locations should Cambridge staff and prospective business owners test before committing resources? The tool screens opportunities; it does not certify unmet demand.

Data collection

Initial collection: 2026-09-21. Cambridge storefront/permit and Boston license data were re-fetched on 2026-09-22 with server-side field selection. Census CBP 2022 and BLS QCEW 2024 Q1 retain their original access date. Cambridge counts and Boston paginated totals are checked against the APIs.

Privacy and cleaning

Cambridge requests use explicit Socrata $select allowlists: snapshot, district, size and vacancy year for storefronts; status, dates and permit type for cottage-food records. Boston CKAN requests use an explicit fields list: license date, category, ZIP and commercial-premises coordinates. Names, contacts, home locations and permit IDs are not requested. Unexpected fields stop the pipeline; there is no full-file fallback. Earlier versions removed sensitive fields before saving; this revision moves exclusion to the source request. District variants are normalized and area ranges use their midpoint.

Measures

Vacant storefronts
Count of rows in the latest available Cambridge snapshot: September 2025.
Estimated vacancy months
Months between the snapshot and the reported vacancy year. Because only a year is provided, July is used as a midpoint assumption and negative values are capped at zero.
Long-term vacancy
A record with an estimated vacancy duration greater than 12 months.
Priority score
District storefront count multiplied by estimated average vacancy months. It ranks outreach urgency; it is not a probability of success.
Area bands
Under 1,000; 1,000–2,500; over 2,500 square feet; or not reported.
Industry context
County-level establishments, employment, and annual payroll for retail, food services, and personal services.

Geographic comparability

Cambridge business districts come directly from the storefront file after label normalization. Boston ZIP codes and coordinates describe food-license records only. Middlesex and Suffolk County statistics provide broad regional context. These three levels are not interchangeable, so the site does not calculate city-to-city vacancy or market-share comparisons.

Market opportunity method

Compare CBP employer establishments and employment for retail (NAICS 44–45), food services (722) and personal services (812). Employees per establishment = employment ÷ establishments, not a staffing requirement. County counts are supply context, not local competitor density; nonemployer businesses are excluded. Do not interpret differences from QCEW as growth because coverage and periods differ.

The editable price/cost model calculates required daily sales = ceiling[fixed monthly costs ÷ (price − variable cost per sale) ÷ trading days]. Inputs are explicitly hypothetical, processed only in the browser, and are not collected demand data. Validate concepts with anonymous preferences and aggregate paid-pilot results before investment.

Reproduce

Run the four fetch/build scripts in pipeline/, then run python3 pipeline/verify_pipeline.py. The website reads only generated JSON and privacy-safe downloadable CSV files. Full commands are in the project README.

Sources: Cambridge Vacant Storefronts; Cottage Food Operations Permits; Boston food establishment licenses; Census CBP; BLS QCEW. Accessed 2026-09-21. Units vary by measure and are defined above.

Methods are designed for auditability and privacy.
